video.title: Fakes: voices, faces and messages
video.format_note: Animated explainer, 16:9, flat Darsi colours on paper-grey backgrounds, one recurring teacher character. Narration in the lesson language; captions as separate files, never burned in.
cast: Ms Amina Bello — primary teacher, Nigeria (main character)
Mr Okafor — Grade 8 science teacher, Nigeria (cameo)
Narrator — the Darsi voice (warm, peer to peer)

chapters.label: A voice note that wasn't him
The lab, and a fake video

scenes.visual: A list: A voice note; Send airtime, now; It wasn't him.
scenes.animation: Each item arrives as it is said.
scenes.narration: On Friday a voice note reached our staff group. It sounded exactly like our head teacher, asking me to send airtime to a new number, urgently. It wasn't him.

scenes.visual: The title card: the course, the lesson title and subtitle, the Darsi mark.
scenes.animation: Mark pops in; the title slides up.
scenes.narration: Today: how AI fakes voices, faces and messages, and a simple routine that beats them.

scenes.visual: A list: A short clip can copy a voice; Faces swapped in photos; Perfect spelling, any language.
scenes.animation: Each item arrives as it is said.
scenes.narration: AI has made fakes cheap. A short clip of someone's voice, from a video or a voice note, can be enough to copy it. Photos can have faces swapped in. And scam messages now come with perfect spelling, in any language.

scenes.visual: A list: Spelling mistakes: gone; Robot voices: fading; Odd hands: fixed; Don't race the glitches.
scenes.animation: Each item arrives as it is said.
scenes.narration: So the old warning signs are fading. Spelling mistakes, robotic voices, strange hands in pictures: each new tool fixes some of them. Hunting for glitches is a race you will lose.

scenes.visual: A list: Pause: urgency is the trick; Call back on the saved number; A code word for money.
scenes.animation: Each item arrives as it is said.
scenes.narration: What does work is a routine. Pause, because urgency is the trick. Check on a channel you already trust: call back on the number you saved, not the one in the message. And agree a code word for anything about money.

scenes.animation: Each item arrives as it is said.
scenes.narration: Here's how it plays out. The fake asks for airtime. You don't reply in that chat. You call the head teacher on his saved number, and he says: that wasn't me.

scenes.visual: The quick check: the question and its answer cards, with the speaker beside them.
scenes.animation: The speaker slides in; answer cards drop in.
scenes.narration: Quick check! A voice note from a new number sounds just like my sister. She says she's stuck and needs money now. What do I do first?

scenes.visual: A list: Call the saved number; A reply reaches the scammer; Ask the family code word.
scenes.animation: Each item arrives as it is said.
scenes.on_screen_text: Call back on a number you trust
scenes.narration: Call her back on the number you saved. A reply in that chat goes straight to the scammer. If you can't reach her, ask for your family's code word, something a fake couldn't know.

scenes.visual: A list: Care for the person first; Don't forward it; Note where it is; Report it to the head teacher.
scenes.animation: Each item arrives as it is said.
scenes.narration: Fakes also hurt people at school. A made-up picture of a pupil or a teacher can spread through a class group in minutes. If it happens: care for the person first, don't forward it, note where it is, and report it to the head teacher.

scenes.visual: A list: A fake of a real person; Can break the law; Always hurts someone.
scenes.animation: Each item arrives as it is said.
scenes.narration: With my pupils, I'm clear: making a fake of a real person is never a joke. It can break the law, and it always hurts someone.

scenes.visual: A list: A call from “IT support”; It needs your code; Authority, hurry, fear.
scenes.animation: Each item arrives as it is said.
scenes.narration: In the app, take a phone call from “IT support” that needs your code. Answer the way many people would, then take the call again and spot the tricks: authority, hurry and fear.

scenes.visual: The quick check: the question and its answer cards, with the speaker beside them.
scenes.animation: The speaker slides in; answer cards drop in.
scenes.narration: Your turn. A video of our head teacher saying school is closed tomorrow is going round. It looks real. What's the best check?

scenes.visual: The summary: Fakes are cheap; Glitches don't last; Pause, call back, code word; Never forward a fake. Takeaway: Trust the routine, not your eyes and ears.
scenes.animation: Points tick in as they are said; the takeaway slides up.
scenes.narration: Check the school's usual channel: a real announcement will be there too. Remember: fakes are cheap and glitches don't last. Pause, call back, and use a code word. And never forward a fake.

scenes.visual: A list: Read a pretend urgent message; Pupils: pause first; Agree a way to check; A family code word.
scenes.animation: Each item arrives as it is said.
scenes.narration: Try it in class tomorrow: play “Pause and check”. Read out a pretend urgent message from someone the class knows. Pupils say what they would do, and the class agrees one way to check, like calling back or a family code word.

checkpoints.feedback_correct: Right: call back on the number you saved. A reply in that chat reaches the scammer.
checkpoints.feedback_wrong: Not quite: a voice can be copied, and a reply goes to the scammer. Call her saved number.
